hints.title: Bottom-Up Label Aggregation
hints.text: In a tree, the count of a label in a subtree is the sum of occurrences of that label across all its child subtrees plus one if the root itself matches.

hints.title: Postorder Frequency Merging
hints.text: Traverse the tree from leaves upward. Each node receives frequency arrays of size 26 from its children and sums them element-wise.

hints.title: Record Node Label Count
hints.text: After summing child frequencies, increment the count for the current nodes label, record it in the answer array, and return the aggregated frequency table.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def countSubTrees(self, n: int, edges: list[list[int]], labels: str) -> list[int]:
        import sys
        sys.setrecursionlimit(200000)
        graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v in edges:
            graph[u].append(v)
            graph[v].append(u)
        ans = [0] * n
        def dfs(u, parent):
            counts = [0] * 26
            u_label = ord(labels[u]) - ord("a")
            counts[u_label] = 1
            for v in graph[u]:
                if v != parent:
                    child_counts = dfs(v, u)
                    for i in range(26):
                        counts[i] += child_counts[i]
            ans[u] = counts[u_label]
            return counts
        dfs(0, -1)
        return ans
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Running a separate traversal per node takes O(N^2) time, which times out for N = 100000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single bottom-up postorder pass passing 26-element frequency arrays takes O(26 * N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate computes answers in postorder traversal returning child frequency distributions.
complexity.notes: Graph is given as undirected edge list with tree root at node 0.
